findings.statement: CD70 has an ADC suitability of 0.746 (rank 2 of 2017), surface score 1.0 with 1 transmembrane segment and 155 extracellular residues; staining_data_available is false, so vital-organ safety cannot be judged. In the weakest quarter of donors 17.7 percent of tumour cells express it (median donor 41.2 percent). It is a known target used as a control.

CA9 has ADC suitability 0.647 (rank 13 of 2017), surface score 1.0, kidney staining level 0.0 but vital-organ staining level 3.0 in stomach; 24.3 percent of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors (median 53.3 percent). It is a known target control; a score does not show a conjugate would work.

ENPP3 has ADC suitability 0.578 (rank 39 of 2017) with 845 extracellular residues, but staining level 3.0 in duodenum and 3.0 in kidney; 21.3 percent of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors. Normal-kidney staining argues for caution.

SCARB1 (top of the target ranking) has ADC suitability 0.558 (rank 51 of 2017), 2 transmembrane segments, staining level 3.0 in adrenal gland and 2.0 in kidney; only 7.1 percent of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors (median 12.4 percent). Not a known ADC target; normal-tissue staining and low per-cell coverage limit it.

SLC16A3 has ADC suitability 0.725 (rank 3 of 2017) and 43.7 percent of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors, but it has 12 transmembrane segments with only 66 extracellular residues and staining level 3.0 in adrenal gland and 2.0 in kidney. A high score does not show an antibody could bind it.

NNMT is a poor ADC candidate: suitability 0.25 (rank 617 of 2017), surface score 0.0 with 0 transmembrane segments, staining level 3.0 in liver and 3.0 in kidney. It is better viewed as a tumour-marker or enzyme target.

CD70 is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab + bevacizumab (log HR per SD -0.383, adjusted p 0.166, n 88) and on sunitinib (-0.262, adjusted p 0.434, n 89); the difference between arms is -0.121 (adjusted p 0.927). None is significant, so these are leads only.

CA9 is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib (log HR per SD -0.336, adjusted p 0.332, n 89) and on atezolizumab + bevacizumab (-0.112, adjusted p 0.665, n 88); between-arm difference 0.224 (adjusted p 0.779). No arm effect is significant.

PCK1 is associated with earlier progression on atezolizumab + bevacizumab (log HR per SD 0.22, adjusted p 0.572, n 88) but slightly longer benefit on sunitinib (-0.069, adjusted p 0.889, n 89); arm difference 0.289 (adjusted p 0.754). Nothing is significant.

PSAT1 has only an atezolizumab arm result (log HR per SD 0.164, adjusted p 0.829, n 86) and the 16-patient nivolumab trial (0.754, adjusted p 0.707), both in the direction of earlier progression with higher expression; neither is significant, and the 16-patient trial gives direction only. No combination or sunitinib estimate was returned.

For NNMT the only trial estimate returned is the 16-patient nivolumab trial (log HR per SD 0.34, adjusted p 0.782, earlier progression with higher expression); no IMmotion150 arm result is available, so treatment relevance cannot be judged.

PSAT1 is higher in BAP1-mutant tumours (CPTAC RNA 1.222, adjusted p 0.011; TCGA RNA 1.711, adjusted p 0.0000578) but the CPTAC protein difference is 0.224 (adjusted p 0.396), so it is not flagged as a subgroup target candidate. ccB minus ccA is 0.541 in protein (adjusted p 0.0000157).

CA9 is flagged as a subgroup target candidate for PBRM1 mutation: mutant minus wild-type 0.971 in CPTAC RNA (adjusted p 0.014), 0.335 in CPTAC protein (adjusted p 0.067) and 1.148 in TCGA RNA (adjusted p 7.18e-7). It is lower in ccB than ccA (protein -0.52, adjusted p 0.000409).
SCARB1 is higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours in RNA (CPTAC 0.614, adjusted p 0.021; TCGA 0.583, adjusted p 2.98e-6) but protein is 0.306 (adjusted p 0.113), so it is not flagged as a subgroup candidate.

EPAS1 defines the ccA/ccB split (defines_the_split true): ccB minus ccA is -0.846 in CPTAC RNA (adjusted p 0.0000501) and -0.935 in TCGA RNA (adjusted p 1.98e-24); no mutation subgroup is flagged. Its only trial estimate is the 16-patient nivolumab trial (log HR per SD -0.236, adjusted p 0.88).

CD70 has an immune-target score of 3.384 (rank 20 of 19161) and 0.654 of its tumour transcripts come from immune cells; rho with CD8 T cells is 0.278 and with regulatory T cells 0.228. Immune-cell expression sits alongside its tumour-cell ADC profile, so the two uses should be separated.

FCGR3A is almost purely immune-derived (immune-cell share 0.999; rho with immune score 0.795, with CD8 T cells 0.457, with M2 macrophages 0.361; immune-target score 3.499, rank 13). Its tumour increase reflects infiltration, not tumour-cell expression.
NNMT is not an immune gene: immune-cell share 0.015, rho with CD8 T cells -0.127, immune-target score 1.515 (rank 5457 of 19161), so its tumour increase is tumour-cell driven.
NNMT cell attribution holds in a second dataset: dominant group RCC in Li 2022 and Zhang 2021 (tumour share 0.97 and 0.948; tumour vs tubule log2FC 9.132 and 5.573; Zhang paired donors 4).

SCARB1 cell attribution does not hold: dominant group is Myeloid in Li 2022 (tumour share 0.336) but RCC in Zhang 2021 (0.582), share-profile Spearman 0.5. Tumour vs tubule log2FC is 3.528 and 4.097, so part of the signal may be non-tumour.
SLC16A3 attribution is inconsistent: dominant group T_NK in Li 2022 (tumour share 0.327) versus RCC in Zhang 2021 (0.809); share-profile Spearman 0.429. Tumour vs tubule log2FC is 6.809 and 6.45.
CA9 is tumour-cell restricted in both datasets: dominant group RCC with tumour share 0.976 in Li 2022 and 0.981 in Zhang 2021; tumour vs tubule log2FC 7.739 and 8.522.

PCK1 is attributed to RCC cells in both datasets (tumour share 0.964 and 0.969); it is lower in tumour than tubule (log2FC -5.787 in Li 2022, -3.044 in Zhang 2021), consistent with loss of a proximal-tubule function.
SCARB1 protein replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort: log2FC 2.334 (adjusted p 3.28e-10, 33 pairs) versus discovery 1.837.
NNMT protein replicates: confirmatory log2FC 4.776 (adjusted p 3.07e-46, 86 pairs) versus discovery 2.709. Absolute fold changes differ by technology.
PSAT1 protein loss replicates: confirmatory log2FC -3.946 (adjusted p 9.71e-23, 69 pairs) versus discovery -1.963. One phosphosite was measured in both cohorts and 0 replicated.
PCK1 protein loss replicates: confirmatory log2FC -4.819 (adjusted p 3.53e-27, 69 pairs) versus discovery -1.859; 2 phosphosites measured in both, 2 replicating.
SLC16A3 protein replicates: confirmatory log2FC 3.551 (adjusted p 1.48e-20, 41 pairs) versus discovery 2.279; 1 phosphosite measured in both and 1 replicating.

caveats: No gene differs between the combination and sunitinib arms after correction; all treatment associations are leads from arms of about 90 patients, and the 16-patient nivolumab trial gives direction only.
ADC suitability scores do not show that a conjugate would work; CD70 has no staining data, and several candidates (ENPP3, SCARB1, SLC16A3, NNMT) stain strongly in kidney or vital organs.

CA9 was not tested in the confirmatory cohort (absent or too sparse, fewer than 10 matched pairs); this is not a failure to replicate. EPAS1 was not run through the ADC, single-cell or confirmatory layers, and the tool returned no combination or sunitinib estimate for NNMT, PSAT1, SCARB1, SLC16A3 or EPAS1.
Subgroup flags rely on mutation calls in small cohorts; immune genes such as FCGR3A can differ only because of infiltration.
Not every requested gene was checked in every layer, because of the call budget.
